units: <cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Ecclesiastes 2:11">Targ. Koh. II, 11</cite>.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Ecclesiastes 9:9">Ib. IX, 9</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 11a:6">B. Kam. 11ᵃ</cite> <he>בדנפשיה ט׳</he> he takes pains with what belongs to himself (for his own benefit).

Ḥull. 83ᵃ דאורח ארעא למִטְרַח וכ׳ in the bridegroom’s family they generally take more trouble in preparing the wedding feast &c.; a. fr. [Sot. 7ᵇ ומטרח, v. טְרִי.]—Part. pass. טָרִיחַ, f. טְרִיחָא giving trouble, troublesome.
<cite ref="Nedarim 25a:14">Ned. 25ᵃ</cite> <he>מילתא דלא ט׳</he> an easily intelligible expression.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 112b:6">B. Mets. 112ᵇ</cite> <he>ט׳ להו מילתא</he> (Ms. M. <he>ליה</he>) it is too troublesome for them (for him); a. e.—[<cite ref="Shabbat 82a">Sabb. 82ᵃ</cite>, v. <cite ref="I00275"><he>טְחַר</he></cite>.]—
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 80b">B. Kam. 80ᵇ</cite> Ar., v. <cite ref="V00972"><he>תְּרַח</he></cite>.

senses.gloss: to make ready for moving, to load (cmp. טָעַן II) Targ. Job XXXVII, 11 (h. text יטריח).).

units: <cite ref="Megillah 22b:13">Meg. 22ᵇ</cite> <he>לא מַטְרַח ציבורא</he> Ms. M. (ed. <he>לא בעי למִיטְרַח</he>, read <he>למַטְרַח</he>, v. Rashi, a. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note) he would not trouble the congregation (to rise before him); <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 669">Yalk. Lev. 669</cite>; a. fr.
<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 16:2">Lev. R. s. 16</cite> <he>א׳ עליה</he> he insisted upon his telling him.—Y. Peah I, 16ᵇ bot. <he>אין מַטְרְחַת עלוי</he> if you strain the chord too much.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Numbers 19:2">Targ. Y. Num. XIX, 2</cite> <he>אִיטְרְחָא</he> (not <he>אַט׳</he>).
<cite ref="Taanit 24b:9">Taan. 24ᵇ</cite> <he>מי איכא דמִיטְּרַה וכ׳</he> is it so hard a labor to the Lord?
